paper_style.palette_strategy: White background with black/gray axes and text; blue/orange compare methods, multi-hue panels distinguish divergences or baselines, and red/gray table text emphasizes gains. Color is often supplemented by panel position, line style, direct labels, or repeated legends, but pastel pairs are not fully grayscale-safe.
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: Charts and tables are primarily native PDF vector/text objects. Figure 4 contains one indexed raster component in its clipping panel; Figure 10 contains ten 464×464 RGB raster scene images. Imported plot labels are Type 3 objects while body/captions use embedded Roman/math fonts.
paper_style.style_consistency: The two-column ICML main body and single-column appendix share caption hierarchy and a restrained palette. Native manuscript typography is consistent, but imported plot labels shift among DejaVu Sans, Arial, and Times New Roman; the smallest labels occur in Figure 4 and Figures 7–11.

figures.label: Figure 1

caption.text: Figure 1. Consistent Average Gains. Results are aggregated over 5 mathematical reasoning benchmarks across 7 LLM scales (spanning both Fast and Slow thinking paradigms) and 10 continuous robotic control tasks. R²VPO consistently achieves the highest average scores, demonstrating its robustness and superiority in both discrete (LLM) and continuous (Robotics) action spaces.

color.semantic_mapping: bar fill identifies Base Model, Clip-Based-algo, and R²VPO; black/gray text carries values and notes

encodings.x: Fast Thinking (3), Slow Thinking (4), and Robot Tasks (10) categories
encodings.text: bar values, absolute gains, and robot random-policy note

figures.data_and_statistics: Grouped bars show average scores aggregated over five mathematical reasoning benchmarks and seven LLM scales or over ten continuous-control tasks. Visible values are 22.17/38.57/40.45 for Fast Thinking, 43.49/48.44/49.49 for Slow Thinking, and 1.27/54.34/65.11 for Robot Tasks; blue/green robot labels show absolute gains of +53.07 and +63.84. No uncertainty, raw task values, or weighting rule is encoded.
figures.evidence_relation: The title-page aggregate result previews the Abstract and introduction claim, then points to Table 2 for LLM macro-averages and Figures 3/11 for task-level control curves. It is headline evidence rather than a mechanism test.
design_strengths: Compact cross-domain scan with direct numeric labels.
Stable bar order and a small method palette make the three-method comparison quick to decode.
The robot random-policy note prevents misreading the near-zero base bar.
design_weaknesses: Accuracy-like scores and robotic reward summaries share one visual scale without normalization detail.
No uncertainty or sample-size display is provided.
Pastel fills and colored gain annotations are weak in grayscale.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a compact grouped-bar headline only when aggregation units and score normalization are stated beside it; retain direct values and add uncertainty rather than relying on color alone.

evidence.label: Title-page Figure 1 grouped averages and caption

figures.label: Figure 2

caption.text: Figure 2. Ratio-variance as a unified proxy for f-divergence trust regions. Theoretical quadratic approximations (dashed lines) align tightly with exact numerical values (solid lines) across Reverse KL, Forward KL, and JS metrics. Boxplots and shading represent 80% confidence intervals from sampled Gaussian policies, confirming that ratio variance provides a stable, computationally tractable alternative to complex divergence constraints.

color.semantic_mapping: panel hue identifies divergence metric; pale trust-region fill and black dashed line identify approximation components

encodings.line: solid exact curve versus dashed quadratic approximation
encodings.facet: Forward KL, Reverse KL, and Jensen–Shannon panels
encodings.text: panel titles and repeated four-item legends

figures.data_and_statistics: Sampled Gaussian-policy updates appear as point clouds; boxplots summarize selected variance bins; pale bands and the caption indicate 80% confidence intervals. Solid curves are exact numerical divergences and dashed curves use the Table 1 second-order coefficients. Sample count and interval construction are not specified, so this diagnoses local alignment rather than global equivalence.
figures.evidence_relation: Proposition 4.1 and Table 1 provide the coefficients, Figure 2 checks three representative divergences empirically, and Theorems 4.3/4.4 state the local-surrogate boundary. Appendix Figure 5 repeats the diagnostic for all six metrics.
design_strengths: Matched axes make exact-versus-approximate behavior comparable across metrics.
Line style, point clouds, boxplots, and bands provide redundant decoding of the diagnostic.
Placement beside the theorem makes the local mechanism easy to connect to the text.
design_weaknesses: Three repeated legends consume plot area.
The 80% interval construction and sample count are absent.
Small points and red/green hues are difficult at print size and in grayscale.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use matched panels for exact-versus-surrogate diagnostics, while reporting sample size, interval construction, and the domain in which the approximation is expected to hold.

evidence.label: Figure 2 three-panel divergence diagnostic and theorem context

caption.text: Figure 3. Training Curves on Continuous Control Tasks (DeepMind Control Suite). We compare R²VPO-ON (blue) against PPO (orange) across locomotion and manipulation tasks, including those with sparse rewards. R²VPO demonstrates superior exploration in sparse settings (e.g., Ball_in_Cup) and prevents the performance collapse observed in PPO (e.g., Cheetah_Run), highlighting the robustness of variance-aware constraints.

figures.label: Figure 8

caption.text: Figure 8. Evolution of Response Length during Training. The dynamics exhibit two distinct patterns: (1) For Fast Thinking models (top row), R²VPO drives a substantial increase in response length, unlocking extended reasoning capabilities. (2) For Slow Thinking models (bottom row), while all methods reduce initial redundancy, R²VPO maintains significantly longer reasoning chains than GRPO (grey line), which often suffers from length collapse. This suggests that variance-aware optimization effectively preserves complex reasoning paths that are otherwise truncated by heuristic clipping.

tables.label: Table 1

caption.text: Table 1. Quadratic approximation of common f-divergences in the trust-region regime (ρθ → 1). All approximations follow the second-order expansion: Df(πθ∥πoff) ≈ f''(1)/2 Varπoff[ρθ].

tables.uncertainty: Deterministic formula dictionary; no empirical uncertainty or missing values.
tables.data_and_statistics: Six rows map each divergence's generator f(u), f''(1), and exact second-order variance approximation. Coefficients are exact symbolic fractions or integers; decimal precision is not substantively meaningful.
tables.evidence_relation: Section 4.1 and Proposition 4.1 lead to Table 1's coefficient mappings, which feed Figure 2's three representative curves and Appendix Figure 5's six-divergence replication.
design_strengths: Exact expressions preserve more meaning than decimal approximations.
The generator → second derivative → proxy columns expose the derivation chain.
Full-width placement gives math-heavy expressions adequate room.
design_weaknesses: The Jensen–Shannon generator is visually crowded.
Notation is dense without a plain-language interpretation.
The expectation distribution behind Var[ρθ] is in adjacent prose rather than the table.
tables.reusable_pattern: For a family of analytical objects, use one exact dictionary table with a stable coefficient column and point readers to an empirical validation object.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: Figures 1–4 move from aggregate cross-domain gain to ratio-variance theory, selected task curves, and mechanism/ablation diagnostics. Figure 5 and Tables 3–4 expand theory, configuration, and benchmark detail; Figures 6–12 and Table 5 add exact-KL dynamics, reward/length/ratio diagnostics, task scenes, failure/stabilization evidence, and runtime. The sequence follows the paper's claim path and appendix calls.
cross_object_system.caption_system: Captions consistently use a small italic Figure/Table label, bold title, setup, and often a conclusion. Figures 2, 3, and 11 are most self-contained because they define encodings or uncertainty; Figures 4 and 5 state strong interpretations while omitting local color, interval, or sampling protocols. Tables describe grouping and primary metrics, but LLM seed/dispersion definitions are absent.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: Result tables name methods and benchmarks explicitly, use grouped headers in Table 2, repeated gray model bands in Table 4, a stable Parameter/Value schema in Table 3, and exact mathematical labels in Table 1. The hierarchy is consistent, although metric direction and aggregation are often left to adjacent prose.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Table 1 and Figures 2/5 establish the variance/f-divergence mechanism, Table 2 and Figures 3/7/11 compare R²VPO with baselines, and Figure 4 plus Figure 6 probe clipping, staleness, λ, ratio distributions, and exact KL. Figure 12 records the high-dimensional failure boundary. The conceptual link is strong, but response length, replay reuse, and performance are not causally separated.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: Appendix objects expand rather than merely duplicate the main story: Figure 5 covers all divergences, Table 3 exposes configurations, Table 4 decomposes Table 2, Figures 6–9 add dynamics/diagnostics, Figures 10–12 expand control tasks and failure, and Table 5 adds infrastructure cost. Calls are visible, but most quantitative detail lives in the appendix.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: Native manuscript text consistently uses Nimbus Roman and Computer Modern math. Imported plot labels use DejaVu Sans, Arial, or Times New Roman Type 3 objects, so typography is internally consistent within plot families but not identical to the manuscript; Figure 4 and Figures 7–11 have the smallest labels.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Blue/orange consistently denote proposed-versus-baseline learning curves in Figures 3, 6, 11, and 12; Figures 7–8 reuse a six-color method legend, divergence panels use metric-specific hues, and Tables 2/4 use red/gray text emphasis. Family-level semantics are good, but no explicit colorblind/grayscale key is provided.

most_reusable_patterns: Lead with a compact headline chart and follow it with matched detailed objects: Figure 1's aggregate groups lead to Table 2/4 and Figures 3/11.
Keep exact-versus-surrogate theory visually parallel: Table 1 → Figure 2 → Figure 5 reuses coefficients, axes, dashed approximations, and distribution overlays.
Use small multiples to preserve heterogeneity: Figures 7–9 and 11 align model/task facets with shared method colors and direct facet labels.
Make negative evidence visible: Figure 12 places vanilla failures and stabilized curves together instead of hiding the intervention.
highest_value_objects: Figure 2 is the clearest local theory diagnostic.
Table 2 is the main LLM decision surface.
Figure 3 gives the most interpretable selected-task dynamics.
Figure 4 connects mechanism, staleness, and adaptive λ.
Figure 11 provides the broadest control-suite visual expansion.
Figure 12 best documents a real applicability boundary.
failure_patterns: LLM tables and Figures 6–9 lack seed/dispersion definitions, so point estimates and trajectories can look more definitive than the protocol supports.
Captions often state a finding while omitting sampling, aggregation, bandwidth, or interval-construction details.
Color is frequently the primary method/metric channel; several pastel or red/green combinations are weak in grayscale.
Runtime is per iteration rather than equal-quality total compute, so the sample-efficiency claim lacks a common compute/rollout denominator.
Public code is implementation-only: no paper TeX, plot scripts, source data, or exact visual assets were found in the matched repository.
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: The paper uses a restrained Roman-text two-column layout and repeated small-multiple/vector diagnostics to move from a ratio-variance headline to local theory, cross-domain curves, mechanism checks, and appendix coverage, but explicit uncertainty/aggregation metadata and public plot/table sources would make the evidence substantially more auditable.
